inline_comments.comment:
The formula `(index % MAX_SECTIONS) - 1` is incorrect and will cause the added tests (and several existing tests) to fail.

When `index % MAX_SECTIONS === 0` — which happens for the very first child (`index = 0`) and again at `index = 12` — the result is `-1`. A section value of `-1` is stored on the node and then used in `flattenNodes` to build the CSS class string `section--1`, which has no matching stylesheet rule. The node will render without any section colouring, reproducing the original bug for a different set of nodes.

The correct formula, which is also what `svgDraw.ts` applies in its own rendering path (line 186: `fullSection % (MAX_SECTIONS - 1)`), is:

```typescript
const childSectionNumber = node.level === 0 ? index % (MAX_SECTIONS - 1) : sectionNumber;
```

This produces values in `[0, 10]` for all non-negative `index` values and wraps exactly at the 12th child (index 11), consistent with every assertion in the new test and the existing `should assign correct section classes` test (where `a0` is at index 0 and expects section 0).

This import creates a downward dependency from the data/DB layer into the SVG rendering layer (`svgDraw.ts`). Normally the rendering layer depends on the DB layer, not the other way around. If `MAX_SECTIONS` needs to be shared between both layers, it should be defined in a neutral location — for example, `mindmapTypes.ts` or a new `mindmapConstants.ts` file — and both `svgDraw.ts` and `mindmapDb.ts` can import from there. This avoids coupling the DB to rendering concerns and prevents potential circular-dependency issues in the future.

The test assertions here are correct — they are consistent with the formula `index % (MAX_SECTIONS - 1)`. However, with the formula as written in the diff (`(index % MAX_SECTIONS) - 1`), `child1` at index 0 receives section `-1`, not `0`, so `expect(child1.section).toBe(0)` will fail immediately. This same mismatch affects `child11` (expects `10`, gets `9`), `child12` (expects `0`, gets `10`), and every subsequent assertion. The test will not pass until the formula in `assignSections` is corrected to `index % (MAX_SECTIONS - 1)`.

general_comments.comment: The formula change in `assignSections` also breaks **existing** tests, not just the new one. The test `should assign correct section classes based on sibling position` checks that `nodeA0` (the first child of root, index 0) has `section === 0`. With `(index % MAX_SECTIONS) - 1`, index 0 yields `-1`, so `expect(nodeA0.section).toBe(0)` fails. Similarly, the edge-section test asserts `edgeA_a0.section === 0` for the same node. Fixing the formula to `index % (MAX_SECTIONS - 1)` resolves all of these failures at once.

The constant `MAX_SECTIONS = 12` is semantically misleading: both the rendering path (`svgDraw.ts` line 186) and the intended DB path use `MAX_SECTIONS - 1 = 11` as the actual modulus, meaning only 11 distinct section indices (0–10) are ever used. Renaming to `NUM_SECTION_STYLES = 11` (and removing the `- 1` adjustments at call sites) would make the code self-documenting and eliminate this recurring off-by-one confusion. This is a pre-existing issue that the PR could have addressed while touching this code.
